Primary Question: What are my active projects?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show the projects I am currently working on.
Alternative Phrasing 2: List my ongoing projects.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT DISTINCT
    p.project_id,
    p.project_unique_id,
    p.project_key,
    p.title,
    p.start_date,
    p.end_date,
    ps.status_name,
    st.stage_name,
    p.priority,
    p.rag
FROM tbl_projects p
JOIN tbl_project_users pu
    ON p.project_id = pu.project_id
JOIN tbl_users u
    ON u.user_id = pu.user_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_status ps
    ON ps.status_id = p.project_status_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_stages st
    ON st.stage_id = p.project_stage_id
WHERE u.email = :current_user  AND pu.request_status = 'A'
  AND pu.status = 1
  AND p.status = 1
  AND p.archive = 0
ORDER BY p.title ASC
Tool Description: Lists the signed-in user's active, non-archived projects via team membership (tbl_project_users), so it includes projects they neither manage nor own. Params: current_user (email). Use get_my_managed_projects or get_my_owned_projects for the PM-only or owner-only views.

Primary Question: Which projects are overdue?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show active projects past their end date.
Alternative Phrasing 2: List delayed projects.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.project_unique_id,
    p.project_key,
    p.title AS project_name,
    p.start_date,
    p.end_date,
    ps.status_name,
    p.priority,
    p.rag,
    DATEDIFF(CURDATE(), p.end_date) AS overdue_days,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.task_id) AS total_tasks,
    SUM(
        CASE
            WHEN t.due_date < CURDATE()
                 AND t.percent_complete < 100
            THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END
    ) AS overdue_tasks
FROM tbl_projects p
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_status ps
    ON ps.status_id = p.project_status_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_tasks t
    ON t.project_id = p.project_id
WHERE
    p.status = 1
    AND p.archive = 0
    AND p.end_date < CURDATE()
GROUP BY
    p.project_id,
    p.project_unique_id,
    p.project_key,
    p.title,
    p.start_date,
    p.end_date,
    ps.status_name,
    p.priority,
    p.rag
ORDER BY
    overdue_days DESC,
    overdue_tasks DESC;
Tool Description: Lists active projects past their end date, with days overdue and overdue task counts. Use for delayed or late projects at portfolio level. Params: as_of_date (the published SQL anchors on CURDATE()). Project-level only - for late tasks use get_at_risk_tasks.

Primary Question: Show active projects for department :department_name.
Alternative Phrasing 1: Which active projects belong to :department_name?
Alternative Phrasing 2: Give me the project portfolio for :department_name.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
-- Resolved 2026-08-27: department membership is via tbl_group_projects + tbl_groups, not tbl_projects.department_id (supersedes the earlier department_id-based reading)
SELECT p.project_id, p.project_unique_id, p.project_key, p.title, p.start_date, p.end_date, p.rag, g.name AS department_name
FROM tbl_group_projects gp
JOIN tbl_groups g ON gp.group_id = g.group_id AND g.status = 1
JOIN tbl_projects p ON p.project_id = gp.project_id
WHERE g.name = :department_name
  AND p.status = 1 AND p.archive = 0
  AND gp.project_id <> 0   -- tbl_group_projects can carry a project_id=0 sentinel row per group
ORDER BY p.end_date, p.title;
Tool Description: Lists active projects in one department. Membership resolves via tbl_group_projects + tbl_groups (authoritative, confirmed 2026-08-27), not tbl_projects.department_id, which returns a different set. Params: department_name (tbl_groups.name). Excludes the project_id = 0 sentinel.

Primary Question: What are my open tasks?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show tasks assigned to me that are not closed.
Alternative Phrasing 2: List my pending work items.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT p.title AS project_title, t.task_id, t.reference_no, t.title AS task_title,
       t.due_date, ts.status_name, t.priority, t.rag, t.percent_complete, tu.allot_percentage
FROM tbl_project_task_users tu
JOIN tbl_project_tasks t ON t.task_id = tu.task_id
JOIN tbl_projects p ON p.project_id = t.project_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_task_status ts ON ts.task_status_id = t.task_status_id
WHERE tu.user_id = :current_user_id
  AND tu.status = 1
  AND t.status = 1 AND t.archive = 0
  AND p.status = 1 AND p.archive = 0
  AND ts.status_type IN (1,2,4,6)   -- open: New/In Progress/UAT/Reopened -- confirm UAT/Reopened treatment with developer
ORDER BY t.due_date, t.reference_no;
Tool Description: Lists open tasks assigned to the signed-in user. Use for 'my tasks' or 'my pending work'. Params: current_user (numeric user_id in the published SQL). Open is resolved via tbl_project_task_status.status_type, never a hardcoded status id.

Primary Question: Compare timesheet hours with task actual hours for :project_name.

SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.project_key,
    p.title AS project_name,
    pt.task_id,
    pt.reference_no,
    pt.title AS task_name,
    pt.actual_hours AS task_actual_hours,
    ROUND(SUM(ts.hours + (ts.minutes / 60)),2) AS timesheet_hours,
    ROUND(SUM(ts.hours + (ts.minutes / 60)) - pt.actual_hours,2) AS variance_hours,
    CASE
        WHEN ROUND(SUM(ts.hours + (ts.minutes / 60)),2) = pt.actual_hours
            THEN 'Matched'
        WHEN ROUND(SUM(ts.hours + (ts.minutes / 60)),2) > pt.actual_hours
            THEN 'Timesheet Greater'
        ELSE 'Task Actual Greater'
    END AS comparison_status
FROM tbl_projects p
INNER JOIN tbl_project_tasks pt
    ON p.project_id = pt.project_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_timesheets ts
    ON pt.task_id = ts.task_id
WHERE
    p.title = 'Project Name'      -- Replace with actual project name
    AND p.status = 1
    AND p.archive = 0
    AND pt.status = 1
    AND pt.archive = 0
GROUP BY
    p.project_id,
    p.project_key,
    p.title,
    pt.task_id,
    pt.reference_no,
    pt.title,
    pt.actual_hours
ORDER BY
    variance_hours DESC;

Alternative Phrasing 2: List users joining projects soon.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
-- Resolved 2026-08-27: allocation_from is not populated in this PMS instance -- this question cannot be answered from the data as it exists today.
SELECT u.user_id, CONCAT_WS(' ', u.first_name, u.last_name) AS employee_name, p.project_id, p.title AS project_title, pu.allocation_from, pu.allocation_to, pu.allocation_hrs, pu.resource_type
FROM tbl_project_users pu
JOIN tbl_projects p ON p.project_id = pu.project_id
JOIN tbl_users u ON u.user_id = pu.user_id
WHERE pu.status = 1 AND pu.request_status IN ('A','I')
  AND pu.allocation_from >= CURRENT_DATE
  AND pu.allocation_from < DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL :days + 1 DAY)
ORDER BY pu.allocation_from, employee_name;
Tool Description: Intended to list users whose allocation starts in the next N days. NOT EXECUTABLE - tbl_project_users.allocation_from is not populated (developer-confirmed 2026-08-27). Params: days.

Primary Question: Who with skill :skill_name is available between :start_date and :end_date?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Find resources with :skill_name and no overlapping allocation.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Show available :skill_name resources.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
-- Resolved 2026-08-27: allocation_from/allocation_to are not populated -- cannot evaluate a date-range overlap.
-- Redefined as "currently has no active allocation at all" (drops :start_date/:end_date from the logic).
SELECT u.user_id, u.username, CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name) AS user_name, us.skill_id
FROM tbl_users u
INNER JOIN tbl_user_skills us ON u.user_id = us.user_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_users pu
    ON u.user_id = pu.user_id
    AND pu.status = 1
    AND pu.request_status = 'A'
WHERE u.enabled = 1 AND u.verified = 1 AND u.is_block = 0
  AND us.status = '1' AND us.skill_id = :skill_id
  AND pu.user_id IS NULL
ORDER BY user_name;
Tool Description: Lists users holding a given skill who currently have no active allocation. Params: skill_name, start_date, end_date. Allocation dates are unpopulated, so availability means no active allocation at all and the date range is not applied - say so when reporting.

Primary Question: Which users have overlapping project allocations?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show resource allocation conflicts.
Alternative Phrasing 2: List people assigned to overlapping project periods.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    pu.user_id,
    CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name) AS user_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT pu.project_id) AS project_count
FROM tbl_project_users pu
INNER JOIN tbl_users u
    ON pu.user_id = u.user_id
WHERE
    pu.status = 1
    AND pu.request_status = 'A'
GROUP BY
    pu.user_id,
    u.first_name,
    u.last_name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT pu.project_id) > 1
ORDER BY
    project_count DESC;
Tool Description: Lists users allocated to more than one active project at once, with a project count. Params: date_range (not honoured). True date overlap cannot be verified - allocation dates are unpopulated. With an explicit count threshold use get_users_over_project_count_threshold.

Primary Question: What is :employee_name’s timesheet utilization for :period?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show logged hours versus available hours for :employee_name.
Alternative Phrasing 2: How utilized is :employee_name based on timesheets?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    u.user_id,
    CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name) AS employee_name,
    SUM(ts.hours) AS total_hours,
    SUM(ts.minutes) AS total_minutes,
    ROUND(SUM(ts.hours) + (SUM(ts.minutes) / 60), 2) AS total_logged_hours
FROM tbl_timesheets ts
INNER JOIN tbl_users u
    ON ts.user_id = u.user_id
WHERE
    CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name) = 'Zubiya Mustafa'   -- Replace with employee name
    AND ts.timesheet_date BETWEEN '2026-08-01' AND '2026-08-31'
GROUP BY
    u.user_id,
    employee_name;
Tool Description: Returns total logged hours for a named employee - the timesheet-based utilisation input. Params: employee_name, period. Unlike get_employee_allocation_utilization this side is genuinely period-scoped; the capacity denominator must still be supplied by the caller.

Primary Question: Show utilization of resources on :project_name.

    u.user_id,
    CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name) AS employee_name,
    SUM(DISTINCT pu.allocation_hrs) AS allocated_hours,

FROM tbl_projects p
INNER JOIN tbl_project_users pu
    ON p.project_id = pu.project_id
INNER JOIN tbl_users u

    AND pu.request_status = 'A'

    u.user_id,
    employee_name

Primary Question: Show utilization for department :department_name in :period.

SELECT g.name AS department_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT pu.user_id) AS total_users,
    COUNT(DISTINCT gp.project_id) AS total_projects,
    SUM(pu.allocation_hrs) AS total_allocated_hours

Primary Question: Show risk creation and closure trend for the last :months months.
Alternative Phrasing 1: How are open risks trending?
Alternative Phrasing 2: Give monthly risk movement.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    DATE_FORMAT(months.month_start, '%Y-%m') AS month,
    COALESCE(created.risks_created, 0) AS risks_created,
    COALESCE(closed.risks_closed, 0) AS risks_closed
FROM
(
    SELECT DATE_FORMAT(date_raised, '%Y-%m-01') AS month_start
    FROM tbl_risk
    WHERE date_raised >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 6 MONTH)

    UNION

    SELECT DATE_FORMAT(date_closed, '%Y-%m-01') AS month_start
    FROM tbl_risk
    WHERE date_closed >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 6 MONTH)
) months

LEFT JOIN
(
    SELECT
        DATE_FORMAT(date_raised, '%Y-%m-01') AS month_start,
        COUNT(*) AS risks_created
    FROM tbl_risk
    WHERE date_raised >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 6 MONTH)
    GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(date_raised, '%Y-%m-01')
) created
ON months.month_start = created.month_start

LEFT JOIN
(
    SELECT
        DATE_FORMAT(date_closed, '%Y-%m-01') AS month_start,
        COUNT(*) AS risks_closed
    FROM tbl_risk
    WHERE date_closed >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 6 MONTH)
    GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(date_closed, '%Y-%m-01')
) closed
ON months.month_start = closed.month_start

ORDER BY months.month_start;
Tool Description: Returns monthly counts of risks created and closed over the last N months. Use for whether risk exposure is trending up or down. Params: months. Closure is derived from status, not date_closed, which stores zero-dates.

Primary Question: Generate a live weekly task summary for :project_name.
Alternative Phrasing 1: Summarise task activity for :project_name between :week_start and :week_end.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Show this week’s task KPIs for :project_name.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,
    task_stats.total_tasks,
    task_stats.open_tasks,          -- status_type IN (1,2,4,6) -- confirm UAT/Reopened treatment with developer
    task_stats.completed_tasks,     -- status_type = 3
    task_stats.high_priority_tasks,
    task_stats.avg_completion,
    task_stats.last_task_update,
    COALESCE(ts_stats.logged_hours, 0) AS logged_hours
FROM tbl_projects p
INNER JOIN (
    SELECT
        t.project_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT t.task_id) AS total_tasks,
        SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type IN (1,2,4,6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_tasks,
        SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_tasks,
        SUM(CASE WHEN t.priority = 'High' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_priority_tasks,
        ROUND(AVG(t.percent_complete), 2) AS avg_completion,
        MAX(t.update_date) AS last_task_update
    FROM tbl_project_tasks t
    LEFT JOIN tbl_project_task_status s ON s.task_status_id = t.task_status_id
    WHERE t.update_date BETWEEN :week_start AND :week_end
       OR t.due_date BETWEEN :week_start AND :week_end
    GROUP BY t.project_id
) task_stats ON task_stats.project_id = p.project_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT t.project_id,
           ROUND(SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)), 2) AS logged_hours
    FROM tbl_project_tasks t
    INNER JOIN tbl_timesheets ts ON ts.task_id = t.task_id
    WHERE ts.timesheet_date BETWEEN :week_start AND :week_end
    GROUP BY t.project_id
) ts_stats ON ts_stats.project_id = p.project_id
WHERE p.status = 1 AND p.archive = 0 AND p.title = :project_name;
Tool Description: Returns a live weekly task KPI summary for one project - total, open, completed, high-priority and overdue counts with the week's effort. Params: project_identifier, week_start, week_end. Dimensions are pre-aggregated in subqueries; open counts status_type IN (1,2,4,6).

Primary Question: Give me a portfolio health summary.
Alternative Phrasing 1: Summarize projects, tasks, risks, and issues.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Show the overall PMS health dashboard.
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tbl_projects WHERE status = 1 AND archive = 0) AS total_projects,
    task_stats.total_tasks,
    task_stats.open_tasks,          -- status_type IN (1,2,4,6): New/In Progress/UAT/Reopened; excludes Closed(3) and Abandoned(5) -- confirm UAT/Reopened treatment with developer
    task_stats.average_task_completion,
    risk_stats.total_risks,
    issue_stats.total_issues,
    issue_stats.open_issues,        -- status_type != 3 (Closed), per C-03
    ts_stats.logged_hours
FROM (
    SELECT
        COUNT(DISTINCT t.task_id) AS total_tasks,
        SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type IN (1,2,4,6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_tasks,
        ROUND(AVG(t.percent_complete), 2) AS average_task_completion
    FROM tbl_project_tasks t
    INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON p.project_id = t.project_id AND p.status = 1 AND p.archive = 0
    LEFT JOIN tbl_project_task_status s ON s.task_status_id = t.task_status_id
    WHERE t.status = 1 AND t.archive = 0
) task_stats,
(
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.risk_id) AS total_risks
    FROM tbl_risk r
    INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON p.project_id = r.project_id AND p.status = 1 AND p.archive = 0
    WHERE r.status = 1
) risk_stats,
(
    SELECT
        COUNT(DISTINCT i.issue_id) AS total_issues,
        SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type != 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_issues
    FROM tbl_project_issues i
    INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON p.project_id = i.project_id AND p.status = 1 AND p.archive = 0
    LEFT JOIN tbl_project_issue_status s ON s.issue_status_id = i.issue_status_id
    WHERE i.status = 1
) issue_stats,
(
    SELECT ROUND(SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)), 2) AS logged_hours
    FROM tbl_timesheets ts
    INNER JOIN tbl_project_tasks t ON t.task_id = ts.task_id
    INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON p.project_id = t.project_id AND p.status = 1 AND p.archive = 0
) ts_stats;
Tool Description: Returns a portfolio-wide health dashboard - active project count with pre-aggregated task, issue and risk counts. Params: current_user_scope, as_of_date. Dimensions are aggregated in subqueries (flat joins would multiply rows). Composition by status is get_active_project_summary.

Primary Question: Which projects are consuming effort faster than they are completing work?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Compare effort burn against delivery completion across the portfolio.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Where is effort consumption outpacing progress?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,
    p.estimate AS estimated_hours,
    p.total_hours_booked,

    ROUND(
        (p.total_hours_booked / NULLIF(p.estimate,0)) * 100,
        2
    ) AS burn_percentage,

    ROUND(AVG(t.percent_complete),2) AS completion_percentage,

    ROUND(SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)),2) AS total_timesheet_hours,

    CASE
        WHEN ROUND((p.total_hours_booked / NULLIF(p.estimate,0))*100,2) >= 80
             AND ROUND(AVG(t.percent_complete),2) < 50
        THEN 'High Burn / Low Completion'
        ELSE 'Normal'
    END AS burn_status

FROM tbl_projects p

LEFT JOIN tbl_project_tasks t
       ON p.project_id = t.project_id
      AND t.status = 1
      AND t.archive = 0

LEFT JOIN tbl_timesheets ts
       ON t.task_id = ts.task_id

WHERE p.status = 1
  AND p.archive = 0
  AND p.start_date <= '2026-08-11'

GROUP BY
    p.project_id,
    p.title,
    p.estimate,
    p.total_hours_booked

ORDER BY burn_percentage DESC;
Tool Description: Lists projects whose effort burn outpaces delivery progress, with burn percentage against average completion. Params: as_of_date, burn_threshold, completion_method. Completion is the unweighted average of task percent_complete - a proxy, not earned value.

Primary Question: Which projects have consumed more than :burn_percent of estimated effort but completed less than :completion_percent of work?

Primary Question: Which project types, business models, sources, or categories have the highest delay and overrun rates?

SELECT
    p.project_type,

    COUNT(DISTINCT p.project_id) AS total_projects,

    SUM(
        CASE
            WHEN p.end_date < CURDATE() THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END
    ) AS overdue_projects,

    ROUND(
        AVG(
            CASE
                WHEN p.estimate > 0
                THEN ((p.total_hours_booked - p.estimate) / p.estimate) * 100
            END
        ),
        2
    ) AS avg_effort_variance,

    COUNT(DISTINCT i.issue_id) AS issue_count,

    COUNT(DISTINCT r.risk_id) AS risk_count

LEFT JOIN tbl_risk r

    AND r.status = 1

WHERE
    p.status = 1
    AND p.archive = 0

GROUP BY
    p.project_type

HAVING
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.project_id) >= 2

ORDER BY
    overdue_projects DESC,
    avg_effort_variance DESC;

Primary Question: Which tasks are due within :days days but remain below :completion_percent complete?

Alternative Phrasing 2: What upcoming work needs immediate action?

SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,
    t.task_id,
    t.reference_no,
    t.title AS task_name,
    t.priority,
    t.rag,

INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON t.project_id = p.project_id

Primary Question: Which projects and tasks have the largest estimate-to-actual effort variance?

SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,
    t.task_id,
    t.reference_no,
    t.title AS task_name,

    CONCAT(u.first_name,' ',u.last_name) AS project_manager,

    c.client_name,

    t.estimate AS estimated_hours,

    ROUND(SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0)+(IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)),2) AS actual_hours,

    ROUND(
        SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0)+(IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60))
        - t.estimate,
        2
    ) AS variance_hours,

    ROUND(
        (
            (
                SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0)+(IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60))
                - t.estimate
            )
            /
            NULLIF(t.estimate,0)
        )*100,
        2
    ) AS variance_percent

FROM tbl_project_tasks t

INNER JOIN tbl_projects p
ON t.project_id=p.project_id

LEFT JOIN tbl_users u
ON p.pm_user_id=u.user_id

LEFT JOIN tbl_clients c
ON p.client_id=c.client_id

LEFT JOIN tbl_timesheets ts
ON t.task_id=ts.task_id

WHERE

t.status=1
AND t.archive=0

AND p.status=1
AND p.archive=0

AND ts.timesheet_date BETWEEN '2026-08-01'
AND '2026-08-31'

GROUP BY

p.project_id,
p.title,
t.task_id,
t.reference_no,
t.title,
u.first_name,
u.last_name,
c.client_name,
t.estimate

ORDER BY
variance_hours DESC

LIMIT 20;

Params: period, top_n, actual_effort_source.

Primary Question: Which tasks show high completion percentages but little or no recent time logged, or heavy time logged with low completion?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Find task progress and effort inconsistencies.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Where does reported completion conflict with timesheet evidence?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,
    t.task_id,
    t.reference_no,
    t.title AS task_name,
    t.priority,
    t.rag,
    t.estimate,
    t.percent_complete,

    ROUND(
        SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)),
        2
    ) AS logged_hours,

    CASE

        WHEN
            t.percent_complete >= 80
            AND
            SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)) < 10

        THEN 'High Completion / Low Time'

        WHEN
            t.percent_complete < 80
            AND
            SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)) >= 10

        THEN 'Low Completion / High Time'

        ELSE 'Consistent'

    END AS mismatch_type

FROM tbl_project_tasks t

INNER JOIN tbl_projects p
ON t.project_id = p.project_id

LEFT JOIN tbl_timesheets ts
ON t.task_id = ts.task_id
AND ts.timesheet_date BETWEEN '2026-08-01'
AND '2026-08-31'

WHERE

t.status = 1
AND t.archive = 0

AND p.status = 1
AND p.archive = 0

GROUP BY

p.project_id,
p.title,
t.task_id,
t.reference_no,
t.title,
t.priority,
t.rag,
t.estimate,
t.percent_complete

HAVING mismatch_type <> 'Consistent'

ORDER BY

logged_hours DESC,
t.percent_complete DESC;

Primary Question: Is the issue backlog increasing or decreasing by project over the last :months months?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show issue creation versus closure trend.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Which projects are accumulating issues faster than they close them?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,
    DATE_FORMAT(i.date_raised, '%Y-%m') AS period,
    COUNT(i.issue_id) AS issues_created,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS issues_closed,      -- was date_closed IS NOT NULL, always-true due to zero-date default
    COUNT(i.issue_id) - SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS net_backlog_change,
    ROUND(
        (SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(i.issue_id), 0)) * 100,
        2
    ) AS closure_ratio
FROM tbl_project_issues i
INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON i.project_id = p.project_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_issue_status s ON s.issue_status_id = i.issue_status_id
WHERE
    p.status = 1
    AND p.archive = 0
    AND i.date_raised >= DATE_SUB(:as_of_date, INTERVAL 6 MONTH)
GROUP BY p.project_id, p.title, DATE_FORMAT(i.date_raised, '%Y-%m')
ORDER BY period, project_name;
Tool Description: Returns per-project monthly issue creation against closure over the last N months, showing whether the backlog is growing. Params: months, time_bucket. Closure uses status_type, not date_closed, which stores zero-dates.

Primary Question: Which projects have the oldest unresolved issues and the slowest closure performance?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Rank projects by issue aging and time to close.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Where is issue resolution performance weakest?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,
    COUNT(i.issue_id) AS total_issues,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type != 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_issues,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.status_type != 3 THEN DATEDIFF(:as_of_date, i.date_raised) END), 2) AS avg_open_issue_age,
    ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.status_type = 3 THEN DATEDIFF(i.date_closed, i.date_raised) END), 2) AS avg_closure_days,
    ROUND(
        (SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(i.issue_id), 0)) * 100,
        2
    ) AS closure_rate
FROM tbl_project_issues i
INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON i.project_id = p.project_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_issue_status s ON s.issue_status_id = i.issue_status_id
WHERE
    p.status = 1
    AND p.archive = 0
    AND (
        i.date_raised BETWEEN :range_start AND :as_of_date
        OR i.date_closed BETWEEN :range_start AND :as_of_date
    )
GROUP BY p.project_id, p.title
HAVING COUNT(i.issue_id) >= 5
ORDER BY avg_open_issue_age DESC, avg_closure_days DESC;
Tool Description: Ranks projects by issue aging and closure performance, with average age of unresolved issues. Use for where issue resolution is slowest. Params: as_of_date, period, minimum_issue_count.

Primary Question: Which projects have the highest defect leakage from earlier origination phases into later detection phases?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show defect leakage by project and phase.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Where are defects being found later than they should be?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT

    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,

    i.defect_origination_phase,
    i.defect_detection_phase,

    COUNT(i.issue_id) AS total_defects,

    SUM(
        CASE
            WHEN i.defect_detection_phase > i.defect_origination_phase
            THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END
    ) AS leaked_defects,

    ROUND(
        (
            SUM(
                CASE
                    WHEN i.defect_detection_phase > i.defect_origination_phase
                    THEN 1
                    ELSE 0
                END
            )
            /
            NULLIF(COUNT(i.issue_id),0)
        )*100,
        2
    ) AS leakage_rate,

    SUM(
        CASE
            WHEN i.severity >= 3
            THEN 1
            ELSE 0
        END
    ) AS high_severity_defects

FROM tbl_project_issues i

INNER JOIN tbl_projects p
ON i.project_id = p.project_id

WHERE

p.status = 1

Primary Question: Which overdue or closed high-severity issues are missing RCA, correction, or corrective-action details?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show issue governance records that are incomplete.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Which major defects lack documented root-cause and prevention actions?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,
    CONCAT(u.first_name,' ',u.last_name) AS project_manager,
    c.client_name,
    i.issue_id,
    i.reference_no,
    i.title AS issue_title,
    i.severity,
    i.date_raised,
    i.date_closed,
    i.planned_closure_date,
    CASE
        WHEN s.status_type != 3 AND i.planned_closure_date <> '0000-00-00 00:00:00' AND i.planned_closure_date < :as_of_date THEN 'Overdue'
        WHEN s.status_type = 3 THEN 'Closed'
        ELSE 'Open'
    END AS issue_status,
    i.rca,
    i.correction,
    i.corrective_action
FROM tbl_project_issues i
INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON i.project_id = p.project_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_users u ON p.pm_user_id = u.user_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_clients c ON p.client_id = c.client_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_issue_status s ON s.issue_status_id = i.issue_status_id
WHERE
    p.status = 1
    AND p.archive = 0
    AND i.severity >= 3
    AND (
        (s.status_type != 3 AND i.planned_closure_date <> '0000-00-00 00:00:00' AND i.planned_closure_date < :as_of_date)
        OR s.status_type = 3
    )
    AND (
        i.rca IS NULL OR i.rca = 0
        OR i.correction IS NULL OR TRIM(i.correction) = ''
        OR i.corrective_action IS NULL OR TRIM(i.corrective_action) = ''
    )
ORDER BY i.severity DESC, i.planned_closure_date, p.title;
Tool Description: Intended to list overdue or closed high-severity issues missing RCA, correction or corrective-action detail. PENDING CLARIFICATION - the severity threshold defining high is not agreed. Params: severity_threshold, as_of_date. Confirm before running the published SQL.

Primary Question: Which risks remain high after mitigation, and which risks have not improved?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Compare original and residual risk scores.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Where has mitigation failed to reduce exposure?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,

    r.risk_id,
    r.reference_no,
    r.title AS risk_title,

    r.rating AS original_risk_score,
    r.after_mitigation_risk_score AS residual_risk_score,

    r.probability_id,
    r.impact_id,

    r.revised_probability,
    r.revised_impact,

    r.owner_id,

    CASE

        WHEN r.after_mitigation_risk_score >= 15
        THEN 'High Residual Risk'

        WHEN r.after_mitigation_risk_score >= r.rating
        THEN 'No Improvement'

        WHEN r.after_mitigation_risk_score < r.rating
        THEN 'Improved'

        ELSE 'Unknown'

    END AS mitigation_status

FROM tbl_risk r

INNER JOIN tbl_projects p
ON r.project_id=p.project_id

WHERE

p.status=1
AND p.archive=0

AND r.status=1

AND
(
        r.after_mitigation_risk_score>=15

        OR

        r.after_mitigation_risk_score>=r.rating
)

ORDER BY

r.after_mitigation_risk_score DESC,
r.rating DESC;
Tool Description: Intended to list risks still high after mitigation and those whose score has not improved, comparing rating with after_mitigation_risk_score. PENDING CLARIFICATION - the residual threshold and the not-improved rule are not agreed. Params: as_of_date, residual_threshold.

Primary Question: Which risk owners carry the largest concentration of high-exposure or overdue risks?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Rank risk owners by unresolved exposure.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Who needs support or escalation for risk closure?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    u.user_id,
    CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name) AS risk_owner,
    SUM(CASE WHEN s.status_type != 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_risks,          -- was COUNT(r.risk_id): counted closed risks too
    SUM(r.rating) AS total_risk_exposure,
    SUM(CASE WHEN r.target_closure_date < :as_of_date AND s.status_type != 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS overdue_risks,  -- was r.date_closed IS NULL, always-false due to zero-date default
    ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF(:as_of_date, r.date_raised)), 2) AS avg_open_age,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.project_id) AS affected_projects,
    SUM(p.deal_value) AS total_deal_value
FROM tbl_risk r
INNER JOIN tbl_users u ON r.owner_id = u.user_id
INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON r.project_id = p.project_id
LEFT JOIN tbl_risk_status s ON s.status_id = r.status_id
WHERE
    r.status = 1
    AND p.status = 1
    AND p.archive = 0
GROUP BY u.user_id, risk_owner
ORDER BY total_risk_exposure DESC, overdue_risks DESC, avg_open_age DESC
LIMIT 10;
Tool Description: Ranks risk owners by their load of open, high-exposure or overdue risks, using summed rating as exposure. Use for escalation routing. Params: as_of_date, top_n. Open is status_type != 2 (1=Open, 2=Closed). For risks with no owner use get_risks_without_owner.

Primary Question: Which resources have the largest mismatch between allocated hours and actual logged effort?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Compare allocation against timesheet consumption.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Who is materially over- or under-consuming their allocation?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
-- Written 2026-08-27: allocation side is CURRENT total (allocation_from/allocation_to not populated); timesheet side is genuinely period-scoped via timesheet_date.
SELECT u.user_id, CONCAT(u.first_name, ' ', u.last_name) AS employee_name,
    SUM(pu.allocation_hrs) AS total_allocated_hours,
    ROUND(SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)), 2) AS total_logged_hours,
    ROUND(SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)) - SUM(pu.allocation_hrs), 2) AS variance_hours
FROM tbl_users u
LEFT JOIN tbl_project_users pu ON pu.user_id = u.user_id AND pu.status = 1 AND pu.request_status = 'A'
LEFT JOIN tbl_timesheets ts ON ts.user_id = u.user_id AND ts.timesheet_date BETWEEN :period_start AND :period_end
WHERE u.enabled = 1 AND u.verified = 1 AND u.is_block = 0
GROUP BY u.user_id, employee_name
HAVING ABS(ROUND(SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)) - SUM(pu.allocation_hrs), 2)) >= :variance_threshold
ORDER BY ABS(variance_hours) DESC;
Tool Description: Compares each user's allocated hours against hours actually logged and returns the variance. Use for whether allocation matches reality. Params: period, variance_threshold. The allocation side is a current total (dates unpopulated); the timesheet side is genuinely period-scoped.

Primary Question: Which resource allocations end before their assigned open tasks or project delivery dates?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show allocation end-date risks.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Where could resources roll off before remaining work is due?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
-- Resolved 2026-08-27: allocation_to is not populated -- comparing it to task/project dates is not possible from this data.
SELECT u.user_id, CONCAT(u.first_name,' ',u.last_name) AS employee_name,
    p.project_id, p.title AS project_name,
    pu.allocation_from, pu.allocation_to,
    pt.task_id, pt.title AS task_name, pt.priority, pt.rag, pt.due_date, p.end_date,
    DATEDIFF(pt.due_date, pu.allocation_to) AS task_gap_days,
    DATEDIFF(p.end_date, pu.allocation_to) AS project_gap_days
FROM tbl_project_users pu
INNER JOIN tbl_users u ON pu.user_id = u.user_id
INNER JOIN tbl_projects p ON pu.project_id = p.project_id
INNER JOIN tbl_project_task_users ptu ON pu.user_id = ptu.user_id
INNER JOIN tbl_project_tasks pt ON ptu.task_id = pt.task_id AND pt.project_id = pu.project_id
WHERE pu.status = 1 AND pu.request_status = 'A'
  AND p.status = 1 AND p.archive = 0
  AND pu.allocation_to IS NOT NULL
  AND pu.allocation_to <= DATE_ADD('2026-08-11', INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  AND (pt.due_date > pu.allocation_to OR p.end_date > pu.allocation_to)
ORDER BY pu.allocation_to, pt.due_date;
Tool Description: Intended to flag allocations ending before their assigned open tasks or the project delivery date. NOT EXECUTABLE - allocation_to is not populated, so no comparison against task or project dates is possible. Params: as_of_date, horizon_days.

Primary Question: What percentage of logged effort is chargeable by project, PM, client, and project type?
Alternative Phrasing 1: Show chargeable versus non-chargeable effort mix.
Alternative Phrasing 2: Where is non-chargeable delivery effort concentrated?
SQL Query (Existing or Recovered):
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.title AS project_name,

    ROUND(SUM(
        CASE
            WHEN t.chargeable = 'Y'
            THEN IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)
            ELSE 0
        END
    ),2) AS chargeable_hours,

    ROUND(SUM(
        IFNULL(ts.hours,0) + (IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)
    ),2) AS total_hours,

    ROUND(
        (
            SUM(
                CASE
                    WHEN t.chargeable='Y'
                    THEN IFNULL(ts.hours,0)+(IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)
                    ELSE 0
                END
            )
            /
            NULLIF(
                SUM(IFNULL(ts.hours,0)+(IFNULL(ts.minutes,0)/60)),
                0
            )
        )*100,
        2
    ) AS chargeable_effort_ratio

FROM tbl_timesheets ts

INNER JOIN tbl_project_tasks t
    ON ts.task_id=t.task_id

INNER JOIN tbl_projects p
    ON t.project_id=p.project_id

WHERE
    p.status=1
    AND p.archive=0

GROUP BY
    p.project_id,
    p.title

ORDER BY
    chargeable_effort_ratio DESC;
Tool Description: Returns the chargeable share of logged effort - chargeable hours, total hours and the ratio - grouped by project, optionally by PM, client or type. Params: period, grouping_dimension. Chargeability comes from tbl_project_tasks.chargeable = 'Y'.
